title: tenant residency decision auditor and rbacv2 telemetry shield
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Customers in regulated geographies requested stronger guarantees that residency decisions (which KMS provider/region is chosen for a tenant) are both auditable and stable across retries, and that RBAC v2 policy decisions are traceable for compliance reviews. This PR adds a tenant residency decision auditor that records immutable decision envelopes to the audit log and introduces a lightweight telemetry shield around RBAC v2 decision paths to prevent sensitive claim material from leaking into high-cardinality metrics.

What this change does (high level):
- Implements a Residency Decision Auditor service that emits signed, immutable audit envelopes for every residency decision taken by the policy router. Envelopes contain a hashed decision payload, resolution path, and signer metadata (no plaintext PII).
- Adds a telemetry shield middleware around rbac-v2 decision engine that scrubs or buckets high-cardinality tokens before emitting telemetry. Shield rules are configurable per-tenant using the existing policy config node.
- Wire-ups to the audit-forwarder: envelopes are enqueued to the existing audit sink and annotated with origin and policy-version tags to support downstream retention/archival rules.
- Integration tests and a small migration to add policy metadata to tenant profiles.

Design notes:
- Auditing: To keep audit logs small while retaining forensics value, the envelope stores a SHA256 of the decision payload and a compact decision trace (sequence of policy checks and short identifiers). The full decision payload can be retrieved via a signed retrieval API (authorization-guarded) for legal requests.
- Signing: Envelopes are signed using the service signing key (rotated by our key manager). Signatures are verified in CI smoke tests.
- Telemetry shield: Shielding rules support three actions: redact, bucket(<n>), and hash. Default for tenant-scoped identity claims is bucket(10) for high-cardinality and redact for long strings (length > 128).
- Backwards compatibility: The residency decision evaluator keeps the existing decision output shape unchanged; the auditor runs as a side-effect and is off by default behind a feature flag and an allowlist for early pilot tenants.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests for evaluator, signer, and shield logic.
- Integration test exercises audit-forwarder enqueue and signature verification (test/integration/residency_audit_e2e_test.go).
- Staged rollout plan: enable feature flag in non-prod for 48 hours, opt-in 3 internal tenants, then gradually enable for customers that signed the residency contract.
- Observability: Added dashboards for audit envelope rates, shield drop counts, and verification failures.

Security & privacy considerations:
- No plaintext customer secrets or full keys are written to audit logs. All sensitive fields are hashed or redacted.
- Retrieval API requires a legal/compliance token and an internal-only service role.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation code
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Docs for operators and runbook entries
- [x] Linear tickets linked
- [x] Feature-flag gating and pilot plan

review_conversation: Miguel Torres: Can you confirm that the envelope size stays < 2KB in the worst-case? We should avoid blowing up audit throughput.
Asha Patel: Measured with synthetic worst-case trace; max envelope ~1.6KB. I added a safeguard to switch to 'hash-only' mode if length > 1.9KB.
Lin Zhao: Telemetry shield looks good, but add a unit test to cover bucket boundaries (bucket(10) vs bucket(100)).
Asha Patel: Added bucket boundary tests and clarified config doc. PTAL.
Connor Hayes: Signed-off on migration approach; ensure retrieval API logs are audited as well.
Miguel Torres: Approved after envelope size check and tests
